label: rem:strangelet-double-beta-interpretation
title: Skein/EM-strong ratio, intermediate $4_1$ state, and observable double-beta signature
html:
Remark. Skein/EM-strong ratio, intermediate 4_1 state, and observable double-beta signature

The Skein amplitude is the EM/strong ratio.

The Skein amplitude s \approx 0.104 is numerically indistinguishable from the EM/strong ratio \tanh(\ln q) \approx 0.104 (crossing energy decomposition). The agreement is structural: both measure the antisymmetric channel of the R-matrix braiding. Each crossing change couples the degree-2 fiber to the degree-1 fiber through the antisymmetric (electromagnetic) channel. The double beta decay rate is therefore

  \Gamma_{2\beta}
   \sim 
  \left(\frac{\text{EM}}{\text{strong}}\right)^4
   \approx  10^{-4}.

The intermediate state.

The path through the Skein resolution tree is:

  T_{2,5}^{\sigma}(5\text{ crossings})
  \xrightarrow{L_0}
  4_1(4\text{ crossings})
  \xrightarrow{L_0}
  T_{2,3}^{\sigma}(3\text{ crossings}).

The intermediate knot is the figure-eight 4_1 — the amphichiral knot identified with the Higgs mass mechanism (building block knots). Its Jones polynomial at q = q_0 is J(4_1) = 1.033, close to 1 (the unknot value). The intermediate state is "almost trivial" — a fleeting Higgs-like excitation between the two beta decays.

The degree-2 to degree-1 fiber transition.

The cinquefoil T_{2,5}^{\sigma} lives on the genus-2 part of Bring's surface: it wraps the surface with winding (2, 5), engaging two of the five sheets. The trefoil T_{2,3}^{\sigma} lives on the genus-1 part: winding (2, 3), engaging the same two sheets but with fewer crossings.

The double beta decay is a fiber descent: the interaction products, born in the genus-2 sector where electromagnetism is absent (Q = 0), cascade through two Skein smoothings to the genus-1 sector where electromagnetism is active (Q \neq 0). Each smoothing peels off one electron-neutrino pair and reduces the crossing number by one.

Observable signature.

The double beta decay of a strangelet interaction produces:

  • Two electrons (or positrons), each from one L_0 smoothing.
  • Two neutrinos (or antineutrinos), one per smoothing.
  • Endpoint energy \sim 2q^{-1} \approx 1.80 Skein units, or approximately 2.3 MeV in physical units (scaling by m_p c^2 / (V_B/\hbar_q^2)).
  • Angular correlation between the two electrons set by the Skein polynomial at the intermediate (4_1) vertex: the figure-eight's amphichirality (4_1 = 4_1^{\sigma}) means the correlation is symmetric under parity.

The 2.3 MeV endpoint and the s^4 \approx 10^{-4} suppression place this in the regime of rare, low-energy electron pair events, detectable in underground experiments designed for double beta decay searches (GERDA, MAJORANA, nEXO, LEGEND). The distinctive prediction: the electron pair spectrum has a parity-symmetric angular distribution (from the amphichiral intermediate) and an endpoint set by q^{-1}, not by a nuclear mass difference.
